finding.claim: Stored SSRF: an attacker-supplied callbackUrl is saved without validation and later POSTed to by the periodic notifyAll job. The attacker can make the server send requests to internal hosts, such as cloud metadata at 169.254.169.254, localhost services and RFC1918 addresses. The request body is the payload, and redirects are not followed by default. The response body is discarded, so this is mostly blind SSRF, but it still allows internal POSTs and port scanning.
finding.sink: HttpClient.send with HttpRequest built from URI.create(cb) (lines 20-24)

trace.note: subscribe(name, callbackUrl) receives the attacker-controlled URL
URL stored in the subscriptions map with no validation
notifyAll iterates the stored callback URLs
URI.create(cb) builds the request URI from the stored value
client.send issues the POST to the attacker-chosen URL

finding.guards_checked: No scheme, host or IP allowlist, no private-range or loopback blocking, and no DNS-resolution check anywhere on the path. The HttpClient is the default one, with no proxy or egress restrictions in this code. URI.create only validates syntax.

verdict.reason: src/Jobs.java:14 stores callbackUrl unvalidated, and src/Jobs.java:21-24 POSTs to it via URI.create and client.send. The only regex guard (line 30) protects thumb(), not this path. No auth or routing code is in the repo, so the endpoint is treated as remotely reachable.
